extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two omnidirectional cameras (Ricoh Theta V) in a vertical top-bottom arrangement and paired with a synchronized LiDAR sensor (Ouster OS1-64) mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Given the sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds compared to high-resolution camera images, ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of the total pixels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 29 video sequences captured in dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes across a university campus under diverse weather and lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline interpolates depth on spherical grid points by using temporally aggregated point clouds. It estimates depth through a weighted average of its k-nearest neighbors and applies a filtering process to exclude points with high uncertainty or lacking nearby measurements.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Temporal aggregation is used to fuse the current frame's point cloud with those from the four preceding and four succeeding frames to increase the number of valid points.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Top images, bottom images, depth maps, and disparity maps are cropped to remove unnecessary borders (sky, ground) and downsized from a width of 1024 pixels to 512 to enable more efficient training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Accurate depth and disparity labels are created by projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images. Initial rotation and translation transformations align the LiDAR points to the camera viewpoint, convert them to spherical coordinates, and project them onto the equirectangular plane.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was assessed by calculating the pixel error by measuring Euclidean distances between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and their image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fully automated depth completion pipeline, KISS-ICP
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images of human pedestrians in dynamic environments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to help build 3D representations of dynamic human environments crucial for navigation and interaction of mobile robots in real-world applications such as autonomous driving, healthcare, or agriculture.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The depth completion approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars and does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries. Indoor-trained models show a clear limitation in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models.
